scope: Two-invocation raw/older-output mechanism check, not a quality/cost optimization trial. Run only after current reuse block ends.
fixture: Identical fresh nonsecret240-record file in both conditions. Read once, run five separate small shell commands, then recover through the supplied CLI if a handle appears and answer the requested record. Never reread the original file.
mechanism_gate: Older-output requests must actually transform an output outside the most recent four; all latest-four fields, tool IDs/status and raw recovery remain intact. Archived source hashes must match exactly. Native per-response input counts must show an effective decrease of at least256 tokens at the first age transform compared with the preceding response, while raw control at the corresponding completed-output boundary does not show that decrease. A byte-only rewrite without effective token reduction is not applied whole-history compression. Verify every request/response count and counter before interpreting.
quality_gate: Both requested fixture values correct. This explicit diagnostic recovery is not autonomous task-performance evidence.
cost: All actual native responses, tool/recovery calls and failures are research expense; report fresh/cached/output and whole-invocation published-rate scenario. Different model action sequences forbid a broad causal savings claim. Effective input drop alone does not imply cheaper inference.
failure: Stop on timeout/ambiguous completion/counter alignment/invalid source recovery; preserve every started call. No retries or repeated started invocation. Unsupported/opaque old history is a failed application gate, not zero savings.
overhead: Both model invocations and all implementation/analysis are research expense, no deployment-saving claim.
rollback: Separate explicit loopback experimental proxy only; normal provider8317 and paused schedules unchanged. Preserve private originals/forwarded requests and raw-source records.
